pages.methodNotes:
Conventions. originX 442.198 px is the left edge of print column 0, and column 0 is this page's leftmost printed column - the head's DATE and the body's LOC field both start there. Absolute printer column numbers cannot be recovered from a photographic reproduction. Deskew of 1.078 deg means the content descends to the right and was corrected by rotating that much counter-clockwise about the point (800, 640) in the original image; the reading strips and every cell measurement come from that deskewed image, never from the rule-suppressed copy.

Slot frame. Slot 0 is the head. The 55 body lines occupy slots 3 to 57 with no interior gap: 56 y-clusters, inter-cluster gaps 14.5-15.7 px, never near the 30.4 px that a skipped slot would give. The head sits 3.046 pitches above the first body line, which is within the 0.830 px worst-case line residual of exactly 3; measuring on cap-top instead of centroid gives the same 3.046.

Form rules. 32 rules from y 120 to y 1064 at 30.4 px pitch, one every two text slots. Found by the margin test: ink in the left margin (x 150-420) AND the right margin (x 1330-1620). A run-length filter cannot work here - dashed rules have a longest run of 4-7 px while the three solid rules at y 182, 273 and 912 reach 328, 546 and 348 px, so any single threshold misses one kind. The rules are not exactly parallel to the text: rule pitch is 30.361 px in the left margin and 30.516 px in the right, so a rule 2.1 px below its neighbouring text line at the left is 2.7 px above it at the right. The mask was therefore built per rule, interpolated between its measured centre at x=285 and at x=1475, thickened by +/-2 px; it covers 12.5 per cent of the page.

Octal sub-layouts. The 12-digit word prints 4-2-1-5 on 54 lines (columns 7-10, 12-13, 15, 17-21). The one TXL line, LOC 00773, prints 1-5-1-5: prefix digit at column 7, decrement at columns 9-13, tag at column 15, address at columns 17-21. Column 11 carries ink on that line and on no other, which is what pins the decrement to 9-13 and so the prefix to column 7.

Fourth field. No line on this page prints a label; all 55 print a +n offset with the plus in column 40 and the digits in 41-42. Columns 30-39 and 43-48 are blank on every content line. Justification cannot be determined from this page: all 55 offsets are two digits (+40 to +94), so there is no one-digit or three-digit case to separate left- from right-justification.

Two lines print no operand at all: LOC 01010 and LOC 01030, both mnemonic COM.

Page head fields: DATE at 0, 10/18/61 at 5, TIME at 15, 2.45 at 21, ACCOUNT at 27 (with no value after it), ID. at 55, CT at 59, PUBLICATIONS at 62, PAGE at 83, 17 at 89.

For a later reader. Deskew on the text but build the rule mask per rule from both margins, or it drifts about 3 px across the page and eats a text line at one end. Include the head line in the advance fit - PAGE 17 at columns 83-90 is what extends the baseline to the full 91 columns. This chain drops strokes in both directions: six zeros lost their right stroke badly enough to read as C, and one lost its left stroke. The strongest verification on an object-listing page is arithmetic, not shape: the shift-count-to-address identity and the CP)+n base identity between them confirmed every digit the template classifier doubted.

I opened none of the banned files. I did not open test/fixtures/90.05-object-listing.target, test/fixtures/90.05-object-listing-notes.md, tool/object_listing_target_source.dart, tool/generate_object_listing_target.dart, comtran-manuals/J28-6169/90.05-sample-program.md, docs/design/m4-codegen.md, docs/design/m1-front-end.md, anything under test/goldens/, or any page scan other than comtran-manuals/J28-6169/images/page-208.png. I also chose not to open comtran-manuals/J28-6169/02-compiler.md, which the task permits, because the only question I might have taken there - what the operand qualifier 8L) means - is a question about this page's value, and I preferred to leave that glyph unsettled on the ink rather than settle it from a document.

Every value in the transcription and the report came from measuring page-208.png with my own scripts, written and run inside my own directory. I read no file another reader wrote and wrote no file outside my directory.

One class of value came from outside the scan, and it is not a reading: the 709/7090 opcode-to-mnemonic correspondences used in the self-check (CAL -0500, LDQ +0560, SLW +0602, ANA -0320, ANS +0320, ORS -0602, LGL -0763, LGR -0765, RQL -0773, ARS +0771, COM +0760, LAC +0535, TXL prefix -3) are my general knowledge of the machine, not taken from any file in this repository. They were used only to check a reading already made from the ink, and every one of them agreed. The same applies to the two dropped-stroke zeros at LOC 01027 and LOC 01030, whose shape favours C: I settled them on the field type plus the mnemonic already read from the ink of the same line, not on any external text.

grid.baselineUsed: print columns 0-90 (grid cells k=43-133, x approx 400 to 1245 px), the full printed width of the page including the head line; NOT the twelve-digit machine-word field. originX 402.82 px is the centre of print column 0, i.e. the leftmost printed cell (the first LOC digit). Underlying fit: cell centre x = 1.9404 + 9.32283*k, and print column c = k - 43, so x = 402.82 + 9.32283*c. Advance found by phase coherence over a=9.0-9.7 px at 0.0001 px steps on 2025 intensity-weighted ink centroids (blobs 3-8 px wide, >=5 rows tall, rule dashes excluded), then least-squares refit on assigned cell indices to a fixed point. Max residual 2.99 px; residual x-slope against y is 4.1e-05 px/px, confirming the deskew.

pages.methodNotes:
For a later page reader of this listing.

1. The text angle is not the page angle. Variance-maximising deskew returns -1.27 deg, which is the angle of 32 pre-printed form rules, not of the text (-1.163 deg). The rules are furniture printed on the stock and the listing is printed on top, so the two carry independent registration; the rules are also slightly bowed, their local slope running from -0.0036 at the top of the page to +0.002 at the bottom. Fit the deskew on text blobs and verify by checking the residual x-error has no slope against y.

2. The rules run at exactly twice the line pitch (30.47 px against 15.2378 px) and every third one is solid, the other two dashed. They fall about 6 px below the centre of every ODD-numbered slot, so odd lines lose their glyph bases and even lines are clean. On a crossed line as few as 9 of the 15 rows in the read band survive. Read doubtful cells from a magnified crop that keeps the rule in place; do not read from a rule-stripped bitmap.

3. Remove the rules by the margin test, with a tolerance for the rule's own tilt. Solid and dashed rules both print in the margins where no text prints; a run-length filter would catch the solid ones and miss the dashed, whose dashes are only about 6 px. But because the rules sit at a different angle from the deskewed text, one rule is not on one image row - it moves about 2 px from margin to margin, so a plain "ink in both margins on the same row" test misses rules. Detect each rule at one margin, measure its intensity-weighted y centroid in the left band and again in the right band, fit y = ic + slope*x through those two clean points, and mask +/-3 rows about that fitted line at every x.

4. The clean rule-only bands on this page are x 300-386 on the left and x 1300-1470 on the right. The left one is narrow and hemmed in: the rules themselves start at x about 288, and eleven upright margin numerals sit at x 279-292 over the lower half of the page (with eleven mirrored show-through numerals at x 1477-1486 over the upper half). Neither set is page text.

5. Fit the character advance over the full printed width. Here it is 9.32283 px over print columns 0-90 from 2025 intensity-weighted centroids; fitting on the twelve-digit machine-word field alone would be a 12-cell baseline. Fit centroids, not left edges. Print column 0 is grid cell k=43, centre x = 402.82 px; cell centre x = 402.82 + 9.32283*c.

6. Whole-glyph correlation is the wrong tool for this font. Mean-subtracted NCC on a mostly-white cell cannot separate 1 from ) or 0 from O - it puts them within 0.01 of each other at r about 0.97. Ink-normalised sum-of-squares with a sub-pixel registration search is much sharper, but two confounds still defeat it, and both bit me before I caught them. First, averaging hundreds of exemplars into a template blurs it through registration jitter, so a sharp glyph then prefers a sparser, sharper template of the wrong character; use leave-one-out and match sample counts. Second, print weight and registration vary across the page width, so an exemplar pool drawn from one side will beat the right answer drawn from the other; match column against column.

7. Prefer a structural feature or an arithmetic cross-check to any shape score. Almost every ambiguity here closed on one of: the top-left flag and centred base bar that distinguish 1 from ) and L and I; the decimal-to-octal identity of SYS)nnn; the constant base 01674 of CP)+n; the tag and decrement echoing the operand suffix; the OCT operand repeating the machine word.

8. Field layout of this page, all in print columns: LOC 0-4, OCTAL 7-21, CNTRL 25-29, offset 39-42 right justified, mnemonic 49-51, operand 56-67. No line prints a label in the offset field; all 55 print a +n offset. The OCTAL field prints the 36-bit word as twelve octal digits in one of three groupings - 4-2-1-5 at columns 7-10, 12-13, 15, 17-21 (37 lines); 1-5-1-5 at columns 7, 9-13, 15, 17-21 (13 lines); and 12 solid digits at columns 7-18 (5 lines, the OCT constants). The head line reads DATE 10/18/61 / TIME 2.45 / ACCOUNT / ID. CT PUBLICATIONS / PAGE 18, with word runs at columns 0-3, 5-12, 15-18, 21-24, 27-33, 55-57, 59-60, 62-73, 83-86, 89-90; its last character in column 90 is the rightmost printed cell on the page.

9. One value on the page is contextually odd and is nevertheless correct as read: slot 6 (LOC 01064, CAL 2)YEAR,2) prints CNTRL 10000 where every other data-name line prints 10001. Verified from the ink, not from the pattern. CNTRL takes three values on the page: 10001 on 23 lines, 10010 on 19, 10000 on 13.

10. The only glyph left open is the first character of the operand BL)2 on slots 38 and 45. Everything else is settled.

pages.methodNotes:
CONVENTIONS THE NUMBERS NEED. originX 437.374 is the x of the CENTRE of print column 0, not its left edge, and it is measured in the deskewed image, not the original. deskewDegrees +1.2658 is the counter-clockwise rotation I APPLIED to the original scan; residual skew after it, measured on the three all-digit fields, is -0.037 deg. The fieldColumns entry for "offset" is 39, the leftmost column any offset reaches (+150); the offset is NOT left-justified. It is right-justified with its units digit fixed at column 42: +150 occupies 39-42, +10 and +25 occupy 40-42, +1 occupies 41-42. The page can tell, because the plus sign moves and the units digit does not. The label field starts at 34 and the longest label on this page runs to column 55.

TWO OCTAL LAYOUTS, BOTH 15 COLUMNS. Instruction words put a four-digit operation code in columns 7-10 and a two-digit flag in 12-13 (45 lines). Prefix words put one digit in column 7 and a five-digit decrement in 9-13 (8 lines). Both put the tag in column 15 and the address in 17-21. A reader who assumes one layout will mis-slice the other.

THE RULES BOW; MASK PER-RULE, NOT BY ROW BAND. 32 form rules, pitch 30.36 px, which is exactly two line pitches, sitting at half-slot offsets in the gaps between alternate content lines. Every third rule is solid, recurring every 91.1 px, that is every six content lines. Fitted slopes sweep smoothly from -0.00215 at the top of the page to +0.00140 at the bottom, 0.20 deg of page bow, so one rule can sit above a content line on the left of the page and cut through it on the right. I fitted each rule as its own line through its margin ink and masked +/-3 px around it across the full width. A row-band mask cannot do this, and nine content lines are crossed by a solid rule that leaves them as few as five clean image rows; every doubtful cell in those lines was read from a crop.

MARGIN TEST, NOT RUN-LENGTH. A row is a rule row when it carries ink in x 330-428 or x 1292-1486 AND spans at least 1000 px. Text spans at most 841 px and never enters either band. This catches the dashed rules (dashes about 6 px, which a 25 px run-length filter keeps) and the solid ones alike. Keep the right band inboard of x 1490: the form prints its own line numerals 1 to 12 upright at x 315-327 on the left and the same numerals rotated 180 degrees at x above 1490 on the right, and both would otherwise trip the test.

DO NOT DESKEW FROM CENTROIDS THAT INCLUDE THE OPERAND FIELD. Commas and parentheses descend and drag the right-hand centroids down; on this page that fabricates +0.093 deg of skew that is not there. Use the projection-variance peak (identical at 1.2665 deg whether run over the whole page or the text band alone), then verify with the all-digit fields only.

DO NOT FIT THE ADVANCE ON HALF THE PAGE. Left half 9.2989 px, right half 9.2446 px, full width 9.2666 px. The halves disagree by 5.0 px, more than half a cell, by print column 90. Ten-column residual means run -0.36, +0.28, +0.33, +0.37, +0.19, -0.19, -0.24 with no monotone trend, so the full-width fit carries no accumulating drift.

COUNT THE FAINT LINES FIRST. Slot 45 carries 99 ink pixels and slot 42 carries 350, against about 1100 for a typical line; a sweep that thresholds on line weight loses both. Both are content. Slot 44's label WITHOLDING.TAX.ROUTINE is 22 characters and runs to column 55, past the mnemonic field at 49, so its instruction (AXT 0) is pushed onto slot 45, which prints no LOC, no octal word, no control number and no label. Slot 42 is a label-only line taking its own slot at the same location as slot 43. Consequence: the location sequence legitimately repeats, and the content-line count exceeds the count of distinct locations.

BUILD THE OCCUPANCY CROSS-CHECK. Rendering the finished reading back onto the column grid and comparing all 5280 cells against measured ink is cheap and it proves the field column numbers and the character positions together. It is the reason I can state the field columns as measured rather than estimated.

A TEMPLATE CLASSIFIER DID NOT WORK HERE AND I DROPPED IT. Three attempts. Fixed cell windows were dominated by neighbour bleed and "disagreed" with 109 readings including the leading zero of 01150. Connected-component isolation cured the bleed but merged glyphs with the rules crossing them, so its 80 disagreements fell almost entirely on the rule-crossed lines. Excluding rule-touched cells left 20 usable exemplars and could not build templates past 0 and 1. The arithmetic self-checks are the stronger instrument on a page like this because they are independent of the ink, and the CP)+n check found a real misread that no shape test flagged.

THE 0-AGAINST-C PROBLEM IS IMPRESSION LOSS, NOT A LETTER. Seven cells, clustered as consecutive lines at one print column (three at column 0, two at column 8, two at column 26). Where the ink decides it decides for zero; where it does not, the field's own arithmetic does. Do not settle these by shape alone in either direction, and expect the same pattern on neighbouring pages.

PAGE HEAD, for whoever needs it: DATE 10/18/61  TIME  2.45  ACCOUNT ... ID. CT PUBLICATIONS ... PAGE  19. Two rules print above it (y 112 and y 142) and one below the last content line (y 1053); all three are furniture.
